THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 06.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA 2360/2015  3  2025:KER:11943  JUDGMENT Dated :6th February, 2025
The 3rd respondent in O.P.(M.V.) No.1029/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-IV, Ernakulam is the appellant.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2. The O.P. was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the wife and 2 children of deceased Asokan, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 03.10.2010.

According to the petitioners, on 03.10.2010, at about 4.00 p.m., while the deceased was riding a motor cycle through Arakkunnam - Piravom public road, a tipper lorry bearing Reg. No. KL-40 B 4430 driven by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit on the motorcycle and as a result of which he fell down sustained serious injuries and later on he succumbed to the injuries, on the same day,
while under treatment.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the tipper lorry.
As per the impugned award, the tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.9,26,000/- and directed the 3rd respondent to deposit the amount.
Aggrieved by the above award the 3 rd respondent preferred this appeal.

sentences.text:
Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

4. Heard Sri.Sebastian Varghese, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Insurance Company/appellant and Sri.Saji P.Joseph the learned counsel for the 1 st respondent, Sri.Vinu Chand, the learned counsel for the 4th respondent and Sri.K.N.Abhilash, the learned counsel for the 5th respondent.
5.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is regarding the income of the deceased as fixed by the Tribunal.

According to them, the deceased was working as mason earning Rs. 15,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.4000/-
6.
It is true that the petitioners could not prove the income of the deceased, as claimed in the OP.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, during the year 2010 will come to Rs.7500/-.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the notional income of the deceased is fixed at Rs.7500/-, for the purpose of computing the loss of dependency.
On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 39 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 15, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was married who left behind 3 dependants, towards personal and living expense, 1/3 of the income is liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).

In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.12,60,000/-
8.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.25000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.80000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.75000/- towards love and affection.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, and each dependent is entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.
Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/- each.
Towards loss of consortium, petitioners together are entitled to get a sum of 2025:KER:11943 Rs.1,45,200/- (48,400 x 3).

9. Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Somwati and Others, (2020) 9 SCC 644.

sentences.text: Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.10000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the petitioners, is on the lower side.
The deceased died in this case on the date of accident.
In the above circumstances, I hold that a compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering would be just and reasonable.
11. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
12. The learned counsel for the 3rd respondent/appellant would argue that in this case 1st respondent did not have any valid driving license at the time of the accident.
Though opportunity was given by the tribunal for the production of the driving license, it was not produced.
Even then the tribunal has not permitted the 3rd respondent to recover the compensation after paying the same to the claimant.
Before this court also, he has not produced valid 2025:KER:11943 driving licence.

13. Even if the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid driving license, the insurer is liable to pay compensation to the 3 rd parties and thereafter they have the right to recover the same from the owner.
In the above circumstances, the tribunal was not justified in denying the prayer of the 3rd respondent to recover the compensation from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent is to be allowed to recover the compensation from the 2nd respondent, after paying the same to the claimant.
14. Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.14,72,500/- as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.
